title: Coherence of the projection formula
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum satisfying the data and axioms of [def-sf-datum]. For every separated finite-type morphism in this datum, the projection transformations of [def-sf-pf]
satisfy: naturality in $K$, $L$, $f$ and the coefficient ring; the identity
for $f=\operatorname{id}$; the associativity pentagon for composable
$f,g$, compatible with the composition law (A4), i.e. the isomorphism
$\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]; independence of the chosen
compactification; the identification with the direct-image projection
formula through $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$; compatibility with base
change, i.e. for a Cartesian square $(f',g',f,g)$ the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Lg^*\bigl(Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\bigr)&\xrightarrow{\ Lg^*\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}\ }&
Lg^*Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L\bigr)\\
{\scriptstyle \operatorname{Ex}_!\otimes1}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle \operatorname{Ex}_!}\\
Rf'_!Lg'^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lg^*L&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{PF}_{f',Lg'^*K,Lg^*L}\ }&
Rf'_!\bigl(Lg'^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf'^*Lg^*L\bigr)
\end{array}
$$

commutes, with $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ the exchange of axiom (A2) and the
vertical arrows read through the monoidality isomorphisms
$Lg^*(M\otimes^LN)\cong Lg^*M\otimes^LLg^*N$ and $Lg'^*Lf^*\cong Lf'^*Lg^*$
(the projection formula commutes with base change); and
compatibility with finite reduction, scalar extension and the pro-étale
realization.

external.place: SGA 4, XVII, §5.2); and compatibility with finite reduction, scalar extension and the pro-étale realization.

proof.text: Use the canonical projection transformations of [def-sf-pf], not mates for the exceptional adjunction. For a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$, [def-exchange-projection] gives precisely $\operatorname{PF}^c=Rp_*(\gamma_j)\circ\pi_p$, where $\pi_p$ is the ordinary pullback/direct-image counit mate. Apply [fix-prop-projection-formula] to this same transformation: its statement gives naturality in $K,L$, compatibility with $\alpha_{g,f}$ (the associativity pentagon), compatibility with the compactification comparisons, and agreement with the direct-image formula for proper $f$. Its operation datum is the underlying datum of [def-sf-datum], so its $K\in D^b_c$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}$ hypotheses hold on the domains in question. In particular these are compatibilities of the actual transformations, not just of the underlying functors or of their invertibility. For $f=\mathrm{id}$ choose $j=p=\mathrm{id}$. The unit, counit, pullback-composition comparison and open projection identification are identities in this normalization, so the displayed composite is the identity. Compactification compatibility then gives the identity in any choice. This uses neither exceptional mates nor a tensor assertion about the proper/open interchange map. At finite coefficients, [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] identifies not only the functors for the compactification $(\operatorname{id},f)$ but also its compact-support exchange with the proper exchange. Thus the proper specialization of the base-change square proved below uses exactly the direct-image exchange named in the statement.

source.place: First paragraph: naturality, identity, pentagon, compactification independence, and proper case

proof.text:
Fix the Cartesian square in the statement and choose $f=pj$ and its base change $f'=p'j'$, writing $h:\overline X'\to\overline X$ and $a:X'\to X$ for the upper base changes. Write $F=Lp^*$, $F'=Lp'^*$, $G=Lg^*$, $H=Lh^*$, $R=Rp_*$, $R'=Rp'_*$. The ordinary adjunctions, including the completed ones at $\mathcal O_E$, are [fix-prop-adjunctions](1); [fix-lem-exchanges] identifies the actual exchanges with their adjunction mates and with the compactification composite. Use the canonical tensor comparisons $\mu$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Unlike mere naturality of $\mu$, its composition clause says that the canonical comparison $\theta:F'G\xrightarrow{\sim}HF$ is monoidal. Explicitly, for objects $A,B$ on $Y$,
$$\mu_{H;FA,FB}\,H(\mu_{F;A,B})\,\theta_{A\otimes B}=(\theta_A\otimes\theta_B)\,\mu_{F';GA,GB}\,F'(\mu_{G;A,B}).$$
Here and below juxtaposition composes right to left and tensors are derived (completed at the integral stage). This equation is obtained by applying the lemma's composition formula to each of the two paths $ph=gp'$ and canceling their common comparison with pullback along that morphism. The lemma states it at every coefficient stage, so this is an equality of integral morphisms as well, not an assertion inferred from their finite reductions. For the integral calculation all intermediate objects are constructible: extension by zero preserves bounded constructibility by [lem-sf-pf-open-factor-coherence](2), including for an input $K\in D^b_c$ without a finite-Tor hypothesis; completed pullback and tensor preserve constructibility by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]; and the proper direct images are constructible by [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]. Hence the all-stage tensor theorem and the constructible adjunctions used below apply to $M=j_!K$, $RM$, $Q=M\otimes FL$ and their base changes.

source.place: Base-change paragraph: canonical pullback, tensor, and square identifications

proof.text: Use $P=FL$, $J=Lj^*$, $J'=Lj'^*$. At finite coefficients [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] says that $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are isomorphisms whose restrictions are identities and that $j'_!$ is fully faithful. At integral coefficients [lem-sf-pf-open-factor-coherence](1)-(3) gives those same facts for the actual completed maps and gives $j_!K\in D^b_c$ without a finite-Tor hypothesis on $K$. Its finite-type hypotheses hold for our compactification. Both routes from $H(j_!K\otimes P)$ to $j'_!(La^*K\otimes J'HP)$ are determined by restriction: identify their source with an object of the image of $j'_!$ using $\mu_H$, $\beta_K$ and $\gamma_{j'}$. The route through $H\gamma_j$ and $\beta_{K\otimes JP}$ restricts to the same identification as the route through $\mu_H$, $\beta_K\otimes1$ and $\gamma_{j'}$, by the pullback-composition/tensor coherence of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Full faithfulness therefore proves the open-factor equality. Rationalization and common-field presentation preserve this equality and its unit identifications by [def-exchange-projection].

source.place: Base-change paragraph: both open-factor routes lie in the image of j′_! and restrict to the identity

proof.text:
For the proper factor let $M=j_!K$, $Q=M\otimes FL$, and set $e_M:\,GRM\to R'HM$. By [def-exchange-projection] its transpose is $\tau_M=H(\varepsilon_M)\circ\theta_{RM}:F'GRM\to HM$. The projection $\pi_p$ is the mate of $(\varepsilon_M\otimes1)\mu_F$, so
$$\varepsilon_Q\,F(\pi_{p;M,L})=(\varepsilon_M\otimes1)\mu_{F;RM,L}.$$
Transpose both routes under $F'\dashv R'$, to the common target $HM\otimes F'GL$. The route using $\pi_{p'}\circ(e_M\otimes1)\circ\mu_G$ transposes, by naturality of $\mu_{F'}$, to
$$(\varepsilon'_{HM}F'e_M\otimes1)\mu_{F';GRM,GL}F'\mu_{G;RM,L}=(\tau_M\otimes1)\mu_{F';GRM,GL}F'\mu_{G;RM,L}.$$
For the other route the transpose, including its target identification, is
$$(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})\mu_{H;M,FL}\,H\varepsilon_Q\,\theta_{RQ}\,F'G(\pi_{p;M,L}).$$
Naturality of $\theta$ moves $F'G\pi_p$ to $HF\pi_p$; insert the preceding counit equation, then use naturality of $\mu_H$ and the monoidality equation in step 2. The result is
$$(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})(H\varepsilon_M\otimes1)(\theta_{RM}\otimes\theta_L)\mu_{F';GRM,GL}F'\mu_{G;RM,L}=(\tau_M\otimes1)\mu_{F';GRM,GL}F'\mu_{G;RM,L}.$$
Thus the transposes coincide, and the adjunction bijection gives equality of the original maps. The mate and triangle identities used here are exactly [fix-prop-adjunctions](1); no exceptional adjunction is involved. The same algebra is valid in the completed integral categories using the completed adjunction and the monoidality already supplied in step 2. It proves integral commutativity directly, without testing equality on finite evaluations.

source.place: Base-change paragraph: proper-factor counit-mate calculation, with both transposes expanded

proof.text: Expand $\operatorname{PF}^c=R(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=R'(\beta)e$ as in [def-exchange-projection]. Apply [lem-sf-pf-compactification-pasting] to these specified maps: its open hypothesis is step 3; its proper hypothesis, with $d=(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})\mu_H$, is step 4. Its target comparison is precisely $La^*JFL\cong J'HFL\xrightarrow{J'\theta_L^{-1}}J'F'GL\cong Lf'^*GL$, so the resulting equality is the displayed square of the item. [fix-lem-exchanges](4) intertwines exchanges with refinement comparisons, and [fix-prop-projection-formula] intertwines the projection maps. Conjugating the proved square therefore gives the compactification-independent square. Naturality in the morphism data follows by applying the naturality assertion of the pasting lemma to these component maps and the square-naturality assertion of [fix-lem-exchanges](1). This proves base-change compatibility directly in the finite and completed categories; field-stage transport is justified in step 6.

source.place: Base-change paragraph: paste the open and proper squares and remove the compactification choice

proof.text: For coefficient changes, [fix-prop-projection-formula] gives finite reduction on its stated finite-Tor domains and scalar extension; the precise finite square is [prop-sf-pf-reduction]. At $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [thm-sf-pf-field] gives the chosen integral representatives, rationalization and common-stage comparisons, with no reduction of a field object to a finite ring. Apply [lem-sf-pf-coefficient-realization-transport] to the comparison functors of (A5) in [def-sf-datum] and the coefficient/site data of [def-exchange-projection]: these supply the primitive-map intertwining and cocycle hypotheses of the lemma. It identifies the image of $\pi_p$ and $R(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ with the specified projection maps, and carries the equal composites proved in steps 3-5 to the corresponding equalities. Functoriality and the comparison cocycles give naturality in the coefficient ring. On the pro-etale finite-Tor domains [thm-sf-pf-proetale] identifies the projection isomorphism with exactly the proper counit projection followed by the open tensor comparison and its completed, rational and common-stage forms. Thus these identities concern the required pro-etale map; integral commutativity was proved before transport.

split_report.summary: Repaired the three returned long steps without changing the statement or Lean record. Step 3 extracts completed open restriction, constructibility and actual-map normalization into a statement-only node, then proves the open factor by restriction. Step 5 cites a conditional typed pasting identity with both pullback/tensor comparisons. Step 6 cites the comparison-intertwining lemma for the four specified unit/counit/open composites. Original steps 1, 2 and 4 and the canonical compactification route are retained. Three new unsplit nodes; no Mathlib leaves or Lean changes.
split_report.blueprint: First paragraph: naturality, identity, pentagon and compactification/proper compatibility (step 1); base-change paragraph: canonical identifications (step 2), open factor (step 3), proper factor (step 4), compactification pasting (step 5); last sentence: coefficient and realization transport (step 6).

tool_uses.why: Independent all-stage projection theorem explicitly supplies composition pentagon, compactification, proper, and coefficient compatibilities; the unit has no other theorem stating these facts.
Generic canonical tensor-pullback coherence, including composition at integral coefficients, needed to compare the transposes; the unit does not state this tool.
Exact open adjunction with invertible unit for arbitrary ring sheaves; used only for fully faithful restriction, not a replacement proof route.
Canonical open-immersion tensor isomorphism is the open factor in the unit’s compactification argument.
Canonical open base-change identification is the other open-factor edge in the unit’s argument.
Completed extension by zero and its actual canonical base-change comparison supply the integral open factor.
Canonical ambient/completed tensor comparison on constructibles fixes the integral open projection normalization.
Identifies the actual exchanges with canonical mates/compactification composites and states refinement and square naturality; needed to identify the arrows in the unit’s square.
Exact sheaf extension/restriction functors descend to derived categories, so their unit/counit identities prove full faithfulness there.
Identifies an open pro-etale topos with the slice; used only for restriction of coefficients and maps.
Sectionwise limits fix the completed coefficient sheaf on the open and restriction of the strict reduction model.
Finite type over the field makes the compactification schemes Noetherian, to check qcqs and quasi-compact open hypotheses.
Checks the quasi-separated hypothesis of the open ring-sheaf lemma.
Checks the domains of completed tensor/pullback for every input of the monoidality theorem.
Checks the domain of the all-stage tensor comparison on proper direct-image objects.
Ordinary sheaf tensor identification over the completed ring sheaf; it fixes the integral open projection map before completion.
Provides flat-term K-flat models on which the open tensor map and its strict quotient construction are computed.
Exact countable products over the completed coefficient sheaf justify the strict product/fiber computation in the integral open normalization.
Termwise products compute derived products once exactness is established; sectionwise sheaf limits alone do not give this.
The functor on strict towers sends the actual identity of reduction diagrams to an identity; no arbitrary cone map or faithful-evaluation claim is used.
Identifies quotient and Koszul completeness respecting their units, so restriction of the strict tower preserves completeness.

Generic localized-ringed-site normalization fixes the finite open beta/gamma and invertible unit used in the unit’s open-factor restriction argument; it supplies no global projection/base-change conclusion.

STEP 1: fix-prop-projection-formula supplies the naturality, alpha-pentagon, compactification and proper clauses. The identity case follows from j=p=id normalizations, and cor-cbc-proper-coincidence identifies Ex_! for proper f. STEP 2: I derived theta-monoidality from the composition clause of lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso. STEP 4: I recomputed both transposes under F'-|R'; both equal (tau_M x 1) mu_{F'} F' mu_G. STEP 3: the source lies in the image of j'_! and j'_! is fully faithful; both routes restrict to mu for ja=hj'. STEP 5: I redid the pasting myself. Naturality of e, then the open hypothesis, gamma_{j'}-naturality, the proper hypothesis and pi_{p'}-naturality give exactly the stated RHS, and the types of z, d and v check. STEP 6: def-exchange-projection and (A5) supply the intertwining and cocycle data. Finite reduction uses only finite-Tor domains via prop-sf-pf-reduction, thm-sf-pf-field uses integral representatives, and thm-sf-pf-proetale identifies the realized map. NEW NODES: all are statement-only, introduce their own objects, carry blueprint.from, and record three kinds of search. They are not duplicates: I ran rg and read the closest nodes (lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison, lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence, lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence). None restates an item clause. I tested the open-factor node on U empty, U=X, n=1 and an infinite-Tor K; its clauses (1)-(3) are true via exact j_!, a qc open, chi levelwise and beta^c from the strict tower. The pasting lemma is a true conditional identity, and the transport lemma is a true formal statement under its hypotheses. There is no cycle.
